title: From Substance Dependence to Self-Reliance
subtitle: Journey Of Rajsamand Rajasthan’s Mukesh Towards Recovery And A Dignified Life Through NAPDDR
body_text: The journey of Mr Mukesh (name changed) reflects how accessible de-addiction services, medical care, counselling and sustained rehabilitation support through NAPDDR, helps individuals rebuild their lives and achieve economic self-reliance. Through National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), the Government of India continues to strengthen de-addiction and rehabilitation services, supporting the vision of a healthier society and a drug-free India. Mukesh, a 39-year-old individual belonging to the Scheduled Tribe community from Rajsamand district of Rajasthan faced significant physical and financial challenges due to substance abuse. The prolonged effects of substance use had affected his physical well-being, causing bodily discomfort and pain in his joints and hands. Coming from a financially vulnerable family, he had received education up to the high school level. His family also faced difficulties in securing adequate housing and meeting basic necessities. Despite these challenges, he aspired to establish himself professionally and improve the living conditions of his family. A significant turning point came on 5 March 2026, when he received assistance from the District De-addiction Centre, Rajsamand, operated by Shubhdeep Group Seva Sansthan, under the NAPDDR framework of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India. The intervention provided him with comprehensive support, including medical consultation, counselling, yoga sessions, nutritious meals, clothing and accommodation. As part of the rehabilitation support, the centre ensured regular and timely meals, daily morning yoga sessions and scheduled medication in the morning, afternoon and evening. Clothing and other essential necessities were also provided free of cost. This structured care and support enabled him to focus on his recovery and gradually work towards rebuilding his life. With the support received through the centre, he moved towards a healthier lifestyle and greater financial stability. Following his recovery, he became engaged in self-employment and now earns a monthly income of ₹12,000, marking an increase of ₹5,000 compared to his earnings before treatment. His improved financial condition has enabled him to contribute towards household expenses and support his family with dignity. The intervention under NAPDDR has played an important role in helping him overcome the challenges associated with substance dependence and move towards social and economic rehabilitation. Beyond medical assistance, the comprehensive support provided by the centre has helped him regain stability, pursue self-employment and work towards a more secure future for his family. **** SS-176-TAR/KV/GA/RK Date: 11.11.2026
